steps.title: Filter internal/bot sessions
steps.description: Decide whether to exclude internal staff/test sessions and/or extremely short bot-like sessions based on is_internal and session_seconds.

options.label: Keep all sessions
options.rationale: Include every session; exclusions might remove genuine edge-case users and introduce bias if the treatment affects who behaves like a bot or internal user.
options.spec: Return the dataframe unchanged; no columns added to ctx.

options.label: Exclude internal sessions
options.rationale: Internal staff and test users are not genuine customers; their behavior may not reflect the treatment effect on real shoppers.

options.label: Exclude bot-like sessions
options.rationale: Extremely short sessions (<10 seconds) are likely bots or accidental clicks; removing them focuses on real shopping attempts.

options.label: Exclude internal and bot-like sessions
options.rationale: Both internal staff and bot-like sessions distort the estimate; removing both yields a cleaner sample of genuine customer sessions.

steps.title: Estimate conversion lift
steps.description: Estimate the average treatment effect on the converted outcome using different regression approaches.

options.label: OLS linear probability model
options.rationale: OLS with HC2 standard errors provides a consistent estimate of the ATE in percentage points and is easy to interpret.
options.spec: Fit OLS: converted ~ C(variant, Treatment(reference='control')) + ctx['covariates']; use HC2 robust SEs; store ATE (percentage points) in estimate, CI in ci_low/ci_high, p-value in p_value; return dict with estimate, ci_low, ci_high, p_value.

options.label: Logistic regression with marginal effects
options.rationale: Logistic regression respects the binary nature of converted; average marginal effect of variant gives the ATE in percentage points.
options.spec: Fit Logit: converted ~ C(variant, Treatment(reference='control')) + ctx['covariates']; compute average marginal effect of variant (treatment vs control) in percentage points using statsmodels.get_margeff(); use HC2 robust SEs for the ATE; store estimate, ci_low, ci_high, p_value; return dict.

data.reason: Excluding internal sessions aligns with common A/B testing practice to focus on genuine customer behavior and avoid contamination from non-representative users.

Adjusting for platform dummies can improve precision by accounting for known prognostic variation in conversion rates across devices, especially if allocation is uneven; this is a common and acceptable covariate adjustment in online experiments.
Excluding internal and bot-like sessions improves measurement validity by focusing on genuine customer behavior; common practice in A/B testing.

Logistic regression with average marginal effects yields the same ATE interpretation as LPM but better respects the binary outcome bounds; widely accepted in econometrics for binary outcomes when marginal effects are reported.
Excluding bot-like sessions (<10s) improves signal-to-noise by removing non-human traffic, a common and justifiable preprocessing step in e-commerce A/B tests.

Adjusting for day and platform is a common precision-improving covariate choice in online experiments; these are pre-treatment, balanced by randomization, and reduce residual variance without biasing the treatment effect.

Skipping explicit dummy creation is acceptable if the modeling step will internally encode categorical variables (e.g., using formula interfaces or automatic encoding), which is common in modern statistical software.

steps.title: Estimate conversion lift
steps.description: Estimate the average treatment effect on the converted outcome using different regression approaches.

options.label: Logistic regression with marginal effects
options.rationale: Logistic regression respects the binary nature of converted; average marginal effect of variant gives the ATE in percentage points.
options.spec: Fit Logit: converted ~ C(variant, Treatment(reference='control')) + ctx['covariates']; compute average marginal effect of variant (treatment vs control) in percentage points using statsmodels.get_margeff(); use HC2 robust SEs for the ATE; store estimate, ci_low, ci_high, p_value; return dict.
options.source: Wooldridge (2010), Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data, Ch. 17
options.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

def estimate(df, ctx):
    data = df.copy()
    variant_dummy = (data['variant'] == 'treatment').astype(float)
    data['variant_treatment'] = variant_dummy
    cols = ['variant_treatment'] + ctx.get('covariates', [])
    X = data[cols]
    X = sm.add_constant(X, has_constant='add')
    y = data['converted'].astype(float)
    model = sm.Logit(y, X)
    result = model.fit(cov_type='HC2', disp=False)
    margeff = result.get_margeff(at='overall', dummy=True)
    me = margeff.margeff[0]
    se = margeff.margeff_se[0]
    z = me / se
    from scipy import stats
    p = 2 * stats.norm.cdf(-abs(z))
    ci_low = me - 1.96 * se
    ci_high = me + 1.96 * se
    n = int(result.nobs)
    return {
        'estimate': float(me),
        'ci_low': float(ci_low),
        'ci_high': float(ci_high),
        'p_value': float(p),
        'n': n
    }

option.label: Logistic regression coefficient (not marginal effect)
option.rationale: Reporting the raw logistic coefficient (log-odds) instead of the average marginal effect may yield a different scale; if non-collapsibility biases the marginal effect, this could alter significance or direction under model misspecification.
option.spec: Fit Logit: converted ~ C(variant, Treatment(reference='control')) + ctx['covariates']; extract the coefficient for variant_treatment; store estimate, ci_low, ci_high, p_value; return dict.

data.reason: Reporting log-odds coefficients instead of marginal effects changes the scale and interpretation, making results incomparable to the estimand (conversion lift in percentage points); marginal effects are required for valid inference on probability differences.

report.narrative: The original analysis estimates a conversion lift of 0.53 percentage points (95% CI 0.14 to 0.92, p = 0.008) and returns a SHIP verdict. The minimal flip changes Filter internal/bot sessions from "Keep all sessions" to "Exclude internal and bot-like sessions". This change is defensible (defensibility 0.85) because both internal staff and bot-like sessions distort the estimate; removing both yields a cleaner sample of genuine customer sessions. The flipped universe estimates a lift of -0.13 percentage points (95% CI -0.50 to 0.24, p = 0.49) and yields a DON'T SHIP verdict. The flip was reproduced by an independent re-execution. Across the 11 explored universes, 5 agree with the original SHIP verdict, giving a design-weighted robustness of 50% (beam-weighted 45%). The filter step is the dominant source of sensitivity: its three options move the estimate by up to 0.67 percentage points and produce 2 of the 6 flipped universes. The covariate step has negligible influence (max absolute delta 0.001) and never flips the verdict. The judge accepted all proposed options for both steps, with defensibilities ranging from 0.75 to 0.85.
caveats: Robustness headline is design-weighted (50%): uniform random sample of the grid: 12 draws (each decision picks each of its options equally), 8 distinct results; independent of the beam search. The share among the explored universes is 45%, but the beam search samples the universes that are closest to flipping, so that figure leans toward flips.
